name.text: Even and Odd Functions — reading symmetry from a graph (JSXGraph)

questiontext.text:
The graph of \(y=k(x)\) is shown below.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="340px"]] (function() { var scenario = {#scenario#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-5, 8, 5, -8], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); var f; if (scenario === 0) { f = function(x){ return 0.3*x*x + 1; }; } // even: symmetric about the y-axis else if (scenario === 1) { f = function(x){ return 0.1*x*x*x - 1.5*x; }; } // odd: half-turn symmetry about the origin else { f = function(x){ return 0.2*x*x + 0.6*x; }; } // neither: axis of symmetry is x = -1.5 board.create('functiongraph', [f, -4.5, 4.5], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Based on the symmetry of the graph, is \(k(x)\) even, odd, or neither?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
An even function's graph is a mirror image of itself across the \(y\)-axis. An odd function's graph looks the same after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about the origin. If neither of these holds, the function is neither. In symbols, an even function satisfies \(k(-x) = k(x)\) and an odd function satisfies \(k(-x) = -k(x)\): the point \((x, y)\) on the graph is matched by \((-x, y)\) for an even function and by \((-x, -y)\) for an odd one.

[[if test="is(scenario=0)"]]

Here the graph is \(y = 0.3x^2 + 1\). Folding along the \(y\)-axis maps it onto itself, so \(k\) is even.

[[elif test="is(scenario=1)"]]

Here the graph is \(y = 0.1x^3 - 1.5x\). A half-turn about the origin maps it onto itself, so \(k\) is odd.

[[else]]

Here the graph is \(y = 0.2x^2 + 0.6x\), a parabola whose line of symmetry is \(x = -1.5\), not the \(y\)-axis. It is not symmetric about the \(y\)-axis and a half-turn about the origin does not map it onto itself, so \(k\) is neither even nor odd.

[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.6 (Even and Odd Functions). Classifies a function as even, odd, or neither purely from the visual symmetry of its JSXGraph-plotted graph, complementing the algebraic-substitution version of this question.

falsefeedback.text: Check carefully: does folding the graph along the \(y\)-axis map it onto itself (even)? Does rotating it through \(180^\circ\) about the origin map it onto itself (odd)? Or neither?
